q: What is the difference between ISO 14064-1 and ISO 14064-2?
title: ISO 14064-1 vs ISO 14064-2
short: ISO 14064-1 is for a company's annual GHG inventory: all emissions and removals inside its boundary. ISO 14064-2 is for a single project: the reductions or removals it achieves against a baseline scenario. Use part 1 to report your footprint and part 2 to claim what one project saved.

ul: ISO 14064-1:2018: absolute emissions and removals of an organisation over a period, usually a year, split into direct and indirect categories.
ISO 14064-2:2019: the difference between a project and its baseline scenario, the emissions that would have happened without it. The result is tonnes reduced or removed, not a footprint.
ISO 14064-3:2019: how a verifier checks either one. It covers verification of past figures and validation of a project plan.
Boundary: part 1 uses organisational and reporting boundaries. Part 2 sets a project boundary and lists the sources, sinks and reservoirs it controls, relates to or affects.
Baseline: part 1 has a base year for tracking change over time. Part 2 needs a baseline scenario, justified and kept conservative.
Monitoring: part 2 asks for a monitoring plan written before the project runs. Part 1 relies on the records you already keep.
Credits: part 2 is a framework only. Carbon programmes such as Verra, Gold Standard or India's CCTS add their own methodologies and additionality tests, and only they issue credits.

sections.h: Do not add a project's savings to your inventory
p: If the project sits inside your own boundary, such as rooftop solar or a boiler fuel switch, the saving already shows up as lower emissions in your part 1 inventory. Subtracting the part 2 figure as well counts it twice. If you sell credits from that project, say so in your inventory report, because a buyer may then claim the same tonnes.

ul: A buyer or lender asks for your footprint: ISO 14064-1, or the GHG Protocol.
You want carbon credits or a verified saving from one investment: ISO 14064-2 with the programme's methodology.
Both: keep one set of meter readings and bills, and use it for each report with its own boundary.

example.title: Illustrative example: 500,000 kWh of rooftop solar used on site
lines: Grid purchase before solar: 2,000,000 kWh; after: 1,500,000 kWh
ISO 14064-2 view: reduction = 500,000 kWh x the baseline factor the methodology sets
At 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25 that is 355,000 kg, about 355 t, the same tonnes already visible in the inventory
example.note: Project methodologies often require the CEA combined margin rather than the weighted average used here; the 0.710 figure is for illustration.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills and fuel invoices and applies the CEA grid factor and IPCC 2006 fuel factors, which gives the activity data behind an ISO 14064-1 inventory and a dated, bill-backed record of before and after for a project.
